description: Osallistumishakemus valokaapeliverkon viankorjaus Pohjois-Suomi Erillisverkot pyytää osallistumishakemuksia valokaapeliverkon viankorjaus- ja dokumentointipalvelua maa- ja sisävesialueilla Pohjois-Suomessa koskevaan hankintaan. Tavoitteena on sopia valokaapeliverkon viankorjauksesta, joka sisältää seuraavat kokonaisuudet: - Viankorjaus - Vikakohteessa vian tarkempi paikallistaminen tarpeen mukaan - Viankorjaustarpeen ajallinen priorisointi sekä resursointi - Korjatun vian/vikapaikan dokumentointi Viankorjauksen vasteaika maa-alueilla: Matka työkohteeseen on tarvittaessa aloitettava kahden (2) tunnin kuluttua Tilaajan Käyttökeskuksen ilmoituksesta. Viankorjauksen vasteaika sisävesialueilla: Viankorjauksista sisävesialueilla sovitaan tapauskohtaisesti. Tilaaja tulee valitsemaan yhden palveluntuottajan, jonka kanssa se tekee sopimuksen. Maantieteellinen jako: Pohjois-Suomi: Lappi, Kainuu ja Pohjois-Pohjanmaa Sopimus ei muodosta tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta. Tilaajalla on oikeus käyttää myös muita toimijoita yksittäisiin viankorjauksiin. Tällaisia tilanteita voi olla esimerkiksi, jos jokin muu toimija kuin sopimuskumppani on jo valmiiksi vikakohteessa ja tilaaja saa näin viankorjauksen nopeammin ja kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisemmin. Hankintamenettelyn tarjousvaiheeseen valitaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät ehdokkaat.,

buyer: Oslo kommune v/ Eiendoms- og byfornyelsesetaten
title: Rammeavtale for strategisk arbeidsplassutvikling og behovsanalyse
description: Eiendoms – og byfornyelsesetaten ønsker å inngå rammeavtale med konsulenter om strategisk arbeidsplassutvikling, behovsanalyser og utarbeidelse av kravspesifikasjoner ved anskaffelse av nye kontorlokaler. Formålet med avtalen er å sikre at kommunen oppnår framtidsrettede, arealeffektive og brukertilpassede lokalløsninger som understøtter virksomhetenes behov, kommunens målsettinger og prinsipper for god arealutnyttelse. Leverandøren skal kunne bistå gjennom hele den tidlige fasen frem til inngåelse av ny leiekontrakt, eller eventuell forlengelse av eksisterende kontrakt. Rammeavtalen kan benyttes av Eiendoms- og byfornyelsesetaten og øvrige bydeler, etater og virksomheter som inngår i Oslo kommune som rettssubjekt. Eiendoms- og byfornyelsesetaten (EBY) er avtaleeier og har ansvar for overordnet forvaltning og oppfølging av rammeavtalen. EBY skal bidra til ensartet og korrekt bruk av avtalen på tvers av Oslo kommune, følge opp avropspraksis, innhente og sammenstille rapportering og følge opp og håndtere forhold som kan ha betydning for rammeavtalen som helhet. Den bestillende virksomheten er ansvarlig for å definere eget behov, utarbeide bestilling, akseptere tilbud og følge opp det enkelte oppdrag. Den bestillende virksomheten er kontraktspart i avropskontrakten og ansvarlig for godkjenning av leveranser, fakturakontroll og oppfølging av eventuelle avvik eller mislighold i oppdraget. Den bestillende virksomheten vil ved behov informere Eiendoms- og byfornyelsesetaten om vesentlige avvik, mislighold eller andre forhold som kan ha betydning for den overordnede forvaltningen av rammeavtalen.

title: Konkurranse om rammeavtaler for rådgivertjenester
description: Fredrikstad kirkelige fellesråd inviterer til åpen anbudskonkurranse om rammeavtaler for rådgivertjenester. Konkurransen gjennomføres etter anskaffelsesforskriften del III. Rammeavtalene skal dekke oppdragsgivers behov for tekniske konsulenttjenester, rådgivning og prosjektering knyttet til den samlede porteføljen av kirkebygg. Formålet er å sikre tilgang til relevant kompetanse ved rehabilitering og vedlikehold, blant annet av kulturhistorisk verdifulle bygg.Oppdrag bestilles ved direkteavrop og kan omfatte både enkeltressurser, større team og avgrensede prosjektoppdrag.Konkurransen er delt inn i tre delkontrakter: Prosjektstyring, tekniske rådgivertjenester samt arkitekttjenester og ansvarlig søker.Det inngås rammeavtale med én leverandør per delkontrakt. Leverandørene kan levere tilbud på én eller flere delkontrakter. Rammeavtalene har en varighet på 2 år + 1 + 1 opsjonsår fra avtaleinngåelsen. Avrop kan inngås etter NS 8401 eller NS 8402, og oppdragsgiver angir aktuell standard i bestillingsskjemaet.

description: Helse Midt-Norge RHF har til hensikt å inngå avtale med en eller to private leverandører om kjøp av spesialiserte rehabiliteringstjenester innenfor tilpasset fysisk aktivitet, for voksne over 30 år. Målgruppen er pasienter med alvorlige funksjonsnedsettelse, uavhengig av diagnose, og behov for spesialiserte, intensive, tverrfaglige habiliterings- eller rehabiliteringstiltak av særlig kompleks art.

title: IK-EØS 026-2026 Rammeavtale for byggevarer til Bergen kommune med samarbeidsparter
description: Bergen kommune og samarbeidspartnere utfører både mindre og større vedlikeholdsarbeider på kommunale bygg. For Bergen kommune ved Etat for bygg og eiendom omfatter dette vedlikehold av bygg lokalisert over hele Bergen kommune. En del av vedlikeholdsarbeidene planlegges og gjennomføres som prosjekter, mens andre oppstår uforutsett og krever umiddelbar utbedring. Arbeidet gjelder både innvendig og utvendig vedlikehold. For å ivareta behov knyttet til ikke-planlagte vedlikeholdsoppgaver skal leverandøren kunne tilby og lagerføre et bredt sortiment av de mest benyttede produktene ved sine utsalgssteder. Sortimentet skal være tilpasset oppdragsgivers behov for rask tilgang til varer og materiell som er nødvendige for løpende drift, vedlikehold og utbedringsarbeider. Produktene som omfattes av denne konkurransen skal være egnet for profesjonell bruk og tilfredsstille relevante lover, forskrifter, standarder og krav til kvalitet, ytelse og dokumentasjon. Produktene skal være tilpasset sitt bruksområde og tåle de belastninger som normalt kan forventes ved drift, vedlikehold og rehabilitering av kommunale bygg og tilhørende uteområder. Leverandøren skal aktivt bidra til å redusere miljøpåvirkningen i leverandørkjeden og arbeide kontinuerlig for å fremme bærekraftige løsninger gjennom hele kontraktsperioden. Dersom det oppstår restleveranser og tilbudt erstatningsprodukt ikke aksepteres av oppdragsgiver, skal de bestilte produktene leveres så snart de er tilgjengelige. Restordre skal fremgå tydelig av ordrebekreftelse og pakkseddel, med opplysning om forventet leveringsdato. Oppdragsgiver ha egne avtaler for verktøy, maling/malingsutstyr, arbeidstøy med verneutstyr, VVS-materiell og kjøkkeninnredninger.

title: Home Contents Insurance 2027 - 2032
description: The Home Contents Insurance scheme in operation through the Housing Service was introduced to give our tenants access to Home Contents Insurance at rates that individually they would not be able to secure. The HCI scheme is available solely for North Lanarkshire Council (NLC) tenants who elect to participate. It is designed to offer a basic pay as you go Home Contents Insurance policy with an option for additional accidental damage cover. Premium payments charged by the insurance providers in this scheme are based on factors such as: - The characteristics of the area - Size of stock - Overall claims experience in the area - The market at the time that the scheme was tendered. As 73%% of our tenants are in receipt of housing benefits or other forms of support for their housing costs, this contract makes the provision of Home Contents insurance more accessible to tenants. Currently circa 5000 tenants subscribe to the scheme.

title: ROKS TP7 : Lot Turbine
description:
Dans le cadre du projet « ROKS-TP7 Centrale de dotation d'Ova Spin », l'installation de dotation, composée d'un groupe de machines comprenant une turbine, un générateur, une vanne sphérique, la conduite forcée et l'unité de contrôle commande datant de la mise en service initiale en 1968, va faire l'objet d'une révision complète après plus de 50 ans de fonctionnement.


L'objectif de cette révision complète de la turbine de dotation est de la mettre à niveau avec l'état actuel de la technique et de la remettre en parfait état mécanique.

La turbine de dotation a fait l’objet d’une révision partielle pour la dernière fois en 2002.


En résumé, les travaux principaux suivants sont prévus :

- Révision complète du générateur existant. Ce point ne fait pas partie de cet appel d’offres, mais fait l’objet d’un lot distinct

- Révision complète de la turbine avec renouvellement intégral de la protection anticorrosion

- Utilisation de la roue de rechange existante, des aubes directrices de rechange ainsi que d’autres pièces de rechange disponibles

- Enlèvement et élimination des peintures contenant des PCB

- Éventuellement, un nouvel échangeur de chaleur pour l'huile du palier de la turbine

- Remplacement de l’ancienne instrumentation


Caractéristiques techniques de la turbine de dotation :

Turbine Francis horizontale

Marque/type : Bell

Débit d'eau : 0,9 m³/s

Hauteur de chute : 57,64 m

Puissance : 500 kW

Mise en service : décembre 1968

Dernière révision : 2002

Vitesse de rotation : 750 tr/min

Puitejärjestelyn perusteella tehtävien toimeksiantojen sisältö, laajuus ja toteutustapa määräytyvät tilaajan kulloisenkin tarpeen mukaisesti. Puitejärjestely ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta, eikä hankintasopimus takaa valituille toimittajille tiettyä hankintamäärää. Kaikki tarjouspyynnössä ilmoitetut määrät ja arviot ovat suuntaa antavia eikä niitä tule tulkita tilaajaa sitoviksi hankintamääriksi. HANKINNAN VAATIMUKSET Hankinnan kohteelle asetetut vähimmäisvaatimukset sekä tarjoajaa, tarjottavia palveluja, asiantuntijoita ja toimeksiantojen toteuttamista koskevat vaatimukset on esitetty tarjouspyynnössä sekä sen liitteissä. title: Belgium – Drilling services – Recompletion of DZH4 – Work-over Rig Services
description: FLUXYS wishes to perform a workover operation on its natural gas storage facility in WUUSTWEZEL (Loenhout), about 30 km from Antwerp near the Dutch border. The subsurface installations of the Underground Gas Storage of Loenhout consist of different types of wells depending on their function and the geological layer they reach: Dinantian Exploitation wells, He1 zone (Cretaceous) monitoring wells, Dinantian Gas Water Contact monitoring wells, Dinantian Peripheral monitoring wells, Namurian monitoring wells, Cretaceous monitoring wells and Eocene monitoring wells. The campaign focuses on one recompletion of a Dinantian Gas Water Contact monitoring well: DZH4. Following a well inspection campaign in 2023, it was found that the well DZH4 was presenting an increased level of corrosion (pittings) on the completion tubings. Therefore 2 recommendations were made: inject corrosion inhibitors in the well similarly to what is made on production / injection wells and replace the completion equipment within a 3-5 years period. FLUXYS has now decided to proceed with these workover operations to change the completion equipment of the well. The preparation and procurement phases of the operations are planned during 2025-2026 with an expected start of operations during Q3 2027.

title: J065-- HVAC upgrades at VA Loch Raven location
description: The contractor will provide all material, labor, equipment, and supervision necessary to complete the above-named project at the VA Maryland Health Care System (VAMHCS), Building 1 Community Living Center (CLC) of the Loch Raven Campus. Primary Deliverables and Project Requirements Covid Ward 2nd floor B wing Upgrade exhaust fans Air Handling Unit (AHU-B) located in attic Replace and upgrade EF-1A and EF-1B for higher CFM outputs Install heat tracing for chillers Wiring and junction box located in room G-15. Chiller located outside CLC in the pit behind the service road. Assess current heat tracing for chill water line. Complete and terminate existing heat tracing wiring to an emergency electrical panel in G-17 in coordination with the VA. Panel selection is TBD. Install a 20-amp GFPE circuit breaker for the heat tracing to the panel selected by the VA. Kitchen basement Replace cooling coil(s) AHU-E located in attic. Replace fan motor AHU-E located in attic. AHU has one fan. New motor must be rated for and capable of sustaining a fan speed of 60Hz. Replace Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) VFD located in the attic and attached to the AHU Replace VFD in kind with Manufacturer (ABB) Controls Integration & Coordination VA has an existing contract with Johnson Controls International (JCI). The contractor shall coordinate with the COR and Facility Maintenance to satisfy necessities for the facility s existing Building Automation System (BAS) controls corresponding to all new work. Contractor will replace/reinstall or provide new hardware or connections for BAS monitoring when required to complete BAS programming or integration. This can include control wiring, modulators, switches, routing, existing equipment etc. These requirements are determined on a case-by-case basis. Testing Adjusting & Balancing (TAB) TAB shall occur after HVAC modifications are made. It must be performed by a certified vendor/contractor per TABB and/or other ANAB accredited programs for standard industry HVAC system performance compliance Contractor shall provide notice to and request attendance of the COR and/or other COR-approved VA representation prior to TAB. A report on the TAB results must be delivered to the COR. TAB report will be reviewed and approved by the VA prior to contractual closeout and final payment Warranty, Operations & Manuals (O&Ms) and Shop Drawings Contractor and/or subcontractor shall provide a warranty letter including point of contact, to the VA. Warranty is based on workmanship, material and equipment. Duration of warranty starts after acceptance and use of new equipment & components O&Ms for all new equipment and other components requiring preventative maintenance shall be provided to the VA. All O&M documents must be received by the VA prior to contractual closeout and final payment Contractor shall provide training to the VA. Shop Drawings All layout changes and new equipment shall be updated in as-builts, shop drawings, manufacturer diagrams, details, where applicable. Due to the nature of the contract, this requirement will be determined based on off application by the COR at completion of work. If no applicable documents are required, then the COR will opt for omission. Assumptions Contractor to provide a cost/unit for each of the deliverable items above and use the total amounts provided for their proposal. Contractor to track the quantities used on their pay applications with any amounts left over being returned to the government after final payment. All deliverables must be received by the VA prior to final payment. Line items will be tracked in every pay application. Financial progress for a line item will be cross-referenced with the corresponding item s physical progress and/or completion status. Misrepresentation of a line item s financial progress may result in rejection from the COR and require the contractor to resubmit the pay application with revision(s). Pay applications must be submitted with a total amount not to exceed the Purchase Order (PO) balance. A contract modification from the Contracting Officer (CO) is required for payment application submissions exceeding the PO balance. Additional work outside of the contract and contractual supplement documents (provided drawings, as-builts, details, existing product information, etc) require authorization and written execution from the CO. Any additional work (quantified via labor, material or equipment) performed/provided by the contractor without guidance from the VA or direction from the CO shall not be included in payment applications. The contractor is committed to working at their own expense and risk under this condition. Supplemental contractual and scope of work include existing as-builts, details and compliance for VA guidelines, federal & state guidelines, applicable codes, etc. VA can provide the contractor with additional available drawings and other documentation. These are considered items pertaining to the original contract s scope of work Standard Inclusions & General Compliance Contractor is responsible for cleaning the work area of trash regardless of if it is their trash or not. This includes areas that other entities may have access to like the attic and mechanical spaces. Contractor is responsible for stewardship of work area and compliance with VA medical facility guidelines. Contractor will adhere to VA-granted permitting requirements and industry standard safety practices including but not limited to: Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) Pre-Construction Risk Assessment (PCRA) Hot or burn work Confined space entry work (if applicable) Lock out tag out (LOTO) procedures PPE Parking at the Loch Raven campus is limited and contractors are subject to facility guidelines for locations of contractor vehicles. Guidance for contractor parking is enforced by the COR, Facility Maintenance Supervisor, Campus Manager, and Deputy Medical Director. Parking outside the campus boundary is not in the VA s jurisdiction The contractor shall coordinate with the facility prior to work that impacts patient care such as shutting down A/C, heating, power or other utilities. Utility and HVAC shutdowns require at least a 14-day written request to the facility per the VA s internal Standard Operating Procedure. Period of performance is 90 calendar days.

title: Perusopetuksen iltapäivätoiminnan hankinta Vantaan kaupungille
description: Perusopetuksen iltapäivätoiminnan hankinta Vantaan kaupungille Vantaan kaupungin hankintayksikkö julkaisee osallistumispyynnön dynaamisen toimittajarekisterin perustamiseksi tämän hankintailmoituksen mukaisesti. Tavoitteena on hankkia perusopetuslain mukainen koululaisten iltapäivätoiminnan järjestäminen oppilaille, jotka ovat oikeutettuja käyttämään palvelua. Perusopetuslain (628/1998) 8 a luvun 48 b §:ssä säädetään aamu- ja iltapäivätoiminnan järjestämisestä ja laajuudesta. Ensimmäisen momentin mukaan kunta voi järjestää ja hankkia tämän lain mukaista aamu- ja iltapäivätoimintaa. Jos kunta järjestää tai hankkii tämän lain mukaista aamu- ja iltapäivätoimintaa, tulee sitä tarjota kunnassa toimivien koulujen ensimmäisen ja toisen vuosiluokan oppilaille sekä muiden vuosiluokkien osalta 17 §:n 2 momentissa tarkoitetuille oppilaille kunnan päättämässä laajuudessa. Perusopetuslain (628/1998) 8 a luvussa määritellyn aamu- ja iltapäivätoiminnan järjestäminen on kunnille vapaaehtoista. Toimintaa voidaan järjestää kunnan omana toimintana, ostopalveluna tai avustettuna toimintana. Vantaan kaupunki järjestää iltapäivätoimintaa avustettuna toimintana siten, että perusopetuksen palvelualue koordinoi, ohjaa ja valvoo iltapäivätoimintaa, mutta varsinaisia toimijoita ovat ulkopuoliset palveluntuottajat. Toiminta katetaan vuosittain opetushallituksesta saatavalla valtionosuudella ja kaupungin osoittamalla määrärahalla sekä huoltajilta perittävillä asiakasmaksuilla. Vantaan kaupungin rahoitus koskee ainoastaan iltapäivätoimintaa. Valituksi tulleilla palveluntuottajilla on kuitenkin oikeus halutessaan järjestää aamutoimintaa koulun tiloissa. Tarkempi kuvaus palvelusta liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Sopimuskausi on määräaikainen ja voimassa neljä (4) vuotta ajalla 1.8.2027 – 31.7.2031. Sopimuksen ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Sopimusluonnos. Sopimukseen liittyy mukautettu dynaaminen menettely, joka on kuvattu tarjouspyynnön kohdassa "Menettely".,

title: Puutavaran puitejärjestely
description: Puutavaran puitejärjestely Hankinnan kohteena ovat Raision seudun koulutuskuntayhtymän rakennusalan koulutuksessa ja työmailla tarvittavat puutavarat ja puutuotteet. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä, johon valitaan enintään kolme (3) toimittajaa. Puitejärjestelyn pääasialliset tuotteet on esitetty liitteessä 2 (Hintalomake). Tarjousten valintaperusteena on halvin kokonaisvertailuhinta. Mikäli hyväksyttäviä tarjouksia saadaan vähemmän kuin kolme (3), valitaan puitejärjestelyyn kaikki tarjouspyynnön vaatimukset täyttävät tarjoajat. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, minkä lisäksi hankintayksiköllä on oikeus kahteen yhden (1) vuoden optiokauteen (1+1). Hankintayksikkö hankkii tuotteita tarpeensa mukaan eikä sitoudu vähimmäisostomääriin. Puitejärjestelyn sisäiset hankinnat on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä 1 (Puitesopimusmalli). Puitesopimus ei muodosta puitesopimustoimittajille yksinoikeutta hankinnan kohteena oleviin toimituksiin. Hankintayksiköllä on perustellusta syystä oikeus hankkia puutuotteita myös tämän puitejärjestelyn ulkopuolelta.,

title: Rammeavtale tømrer, malerarbeid og gulvlegging.
description: Bakgrunn Bustadstiftinga skal inngå en ny rammeavtale for tømrer arbeid, malerarbeid og gulvlegging ettersom eksisterende avtale er utløpt. Bygningsmassen krever løpende vedlikehold og reparasjoner, og virksomheten har behov for en forutsigbar og tilgjengelig leverandør som kan håndtere et stort antall mindre oppdrag gjennom året. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å sikre rask og effektiv håndtering av planlagte vedlikeholdsoppgaver og uforutsette skader på bygg og overflater, slik at eiendommene holdes i forsvarlig stand og beboerne berøres minst mulig. Rammeavtalen skal bidra til kort responstid ved behov, samt en enkel bestillings- og oppfølgings prosess gjennom ett fast kontaktpunkt. Beskrivelse av oppdraget Oppdraget omfatter etablering av en rammeavtale for utførelse av tømrer arbeider med tilhørende gulvlegger- og malerarbeider i Bustadstiftingas bygningsmasse. Avtalen skal dekke en kombinasjon av løpende mindre reparasjoner, skade utbedringer og planlagt vedlikehold, samt arbeider i forbindelse med flytting og mindre ombygginger. Leveransen skal være helhetlig og omfatte nødvendige ressurser og innsatsfaktorer for å gjennomføre oppdragene, herunder arbeid og materialer, praktisk tilrettelegging og logistikk på stedet, samt håndtering av avfall og slutt rengjøring etter utført arbeid. Etter gjennomføring skal relevante opplysninger og dokumentasjon knyttet til leveransen overleveres til oppdragsgiver. Rammeavtalen er primært innrettet mot små og mellomstore enkeltoppdrag som bestilles fortløpende, og hvor det er behov for fleksibilitet, effektiv gjennomføring og dokumenterbar kvalitet i utførelsen. Bustadstiftinga forbeholder seg retten til å innhente priser på enkelt arbeider som overstiger NOK 300 000,-.

https://www.epfl.ch/about/philanthropy/fr/soutien-aux-nouveaux-batiments/advanced-science-building/.

title: Belgium – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – CEFTA TRACES NT Maintenance, Expansion and SPS Digital Systems Support
description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. title: Small Arms Range Construction Pease ANGB
description: This notice constitutes an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Solicitation W50S8A-27-B-A002 for the construction of a Small Arms Range at Pease Air National Guard Base (ANGB) in Newington, NH. The Government seeks to award a single firm fixed price contract for services, non-person, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools equipment, appliances and supervisors needed to for the demolition of an existing range on that site and the construction of a new range facility according to the plans, designs, drawings, and specifications. The anticipated contract duration shall be 455 days after the notice to proceed. Please refer to the attached SF1442 for a complete listing of applicable provisions and clauses. Also note that the Government is setting this requirement aside as a total 100% small business set aside under NAICS 236220 which has a small business size standard of $45.0M. The associated PSC is Y1JZ.Interested parties shall provide their bids to the Government by the closing and time of this solicitation and shall be available for public opening at the time and date specified in Block 13 of the SF1442. Bids shall be either submitted electronically via the solicitation module in PIEE or hand carried to the Portsmouth Armory on opening day. The Government will not accept bid submission by any other means. Interested bidders are strongly encouraged to review the instructions to Bidders in section 00 21 00 of the solicitation. This posting also constitutes a notice of pre-bid conference and site visit which the Government will conduct on December 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM (EST) on-site at Pease ANGB in Newington, NH. Please see paragraph 4 of section 00 21 00 for details regarding site access. Interested parties shall note that there exists a brand-specific aspect to this requirement. Specifically, the newly constructed range must have Monaco fire-alarm components. See the attached brand name justification for full details. In accordance with FAR 36.211(b), the following information is provided: (1) The National Guard has no agency-specific policies or procedures applicable to definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts other than those described at FAR 43.204, DFARS 243.204 and AFARS 5143.204.(2) Data for the prior 3 fiscal years regarding the time required to definitize equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts for the National Guard is currently not available but will be compiled and provided in future announcements.

title: Fenêtres et portes-fenêtres - Rénovation du bâtiment PICTO Avenue Ernest-Pictet 28-30
description:
Le présent marché porte sur les travaux de fenêtres et de portes-fenêtres dans le cadre de la rénovation et de la transformation du bâtiment PICTO, situé avenue Ernest-Pictet 28–30 à Genève.

Les prestations comprennent notamment la fourniture et la pose de fenêtres et de portes-fenêtres en remplacement des éléments existants, y compris les cadres, les vitrages, la quincaillerie, les entrées d’air, les tablettes de fenêtre intérieures, les raccords d’étanchéité à l’air et à l’eau avec la façade, ainsi que les finitions de pose. Le marché comprend l’ensemble des travaux, fournitures, protections, essais, contrôles et mises en service nécessaires à la réalisation complète des ouvrages.

Les travaux seront réalisés en coordination avec les autres corps de métier intervenant dans le cadre de la rénovation du bâtiment.

buyer: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board
title: Pre Front Door Integrated Urgent Care Services
description:
NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (CW ICB) are seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced providers for the provision of a comprehensive Pre-Front Door Integrated Urgent Care (IUC) model across Coventry and Warwickshire.

This model requires a single, accountable Lead Provider in each of the two geographical areas:
Coventry (Lot 1) and
Warwickshire (Lot 2)

The appointed Lead Providers will be responsible for the end-to-end design, mobilisation, delivery, clinical governance and continuous improvement of a whole-system urgent care pathway spanning NHS 111 interfaces, GP out of hours, UTC/MIU, ambulance conveyance alternatives, Emergency Department front-door streaming, same-day emergency care, diagnostics, community response and neighbourhood urgent care pathways.

The ICB is not seeking a provider of isolated urgent care components. It is seeking an organisation with the scale, capability, and system leadership to deliver an integrated Lead Provider model. Providers must therefore bring together all interdependent services, healthcare professionals and current Providers, including urgent primary care, community response, and mental health crisis interfaces, into a coherent, accountable and high-performing model.

Contract Length is expected to be 5 years, commencing 1st September 2027 with the Commissioner having the option to extend the Contract for up to a further 5 years.

Further details are provided in VI.3

title: MSG Cook Services Lisbon - Portugal
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States of America in Lisbon, Portugal will launch the solicitation on the beta.SAM.gov website. The Embassy of the United States of America in Lisbon, Portugal, intends to issue a solicitation for cooking/food services for the Marine Security Guards. Brief Summary of Work - The Contractor shall provide cooking services for seven (7) Marine Security Guards (MSG). Contractor shall schedule cooking and serving requirements to ensure that these are done in the order and time frame specified and they are to be performed daily, Monday-Friday. Breakfast (from 7:00-9:30am), Lunch (11:00am to 1:30pm) and Dinner (4:30-7:30pm). The Contractor must clean the kitchen, all dishes and appliances after each meal and cause minimal disruption to the normal operation of the facility. The COR (Contracting Officer Representative) shall determine the schedules presented which will meet the needs of the individual facility. All services are to be delivered for 7 of USG Marine security personnel in providing 7 (seven) meals (2 breakfast options, 2 lunch options and 3 dinner options) at the MSGR for U.S. Embassy Lisbon. Groceries: All groceries and ingredients shall be purchased by MSG within a prescribed budget. Contractor shall coordinate with MSG for required items. The anticipated performance period is for a 6 months base year, with one-year option period, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the lowest priced technically acceptable offeror who is a responsible contractor. The Government may award the contract based on the initial offer without discussion. The resultant contract will be a firm fixed price type contract. The Government is planning to hold a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be announced in the solicitation. All contractors have to be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to contract award pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. Interested parties should contact: Embassy of the United States of America Attn: GSO/Procurement Email: LisbonProcure@state.gov Tel: +351 21 770 2507

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. title: Accessories for Keysight N5242A
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The United States Air Force (AFLCMC/AFMETCAL) is seeking sources to procure and deliver modernized, fully compatible accessories to support legacy Keysight N5242A Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs). The scope of this effort encompasses the delivery of plug-and-play replacement accessories and physical standards to numerous designated Precision Measurement Equipment Laboratories (PMELs) across the Air Force enterprise. Prospective contractors must demonstrate the technical capability to supply highly specialized, high-precision radio frequency (RF) and microwave calibration accessories that integrate seamlessly with the existing N5242A VNA platform without requiring software modifications or degrading established metrological accuracy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 1 unit over 1 year. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27E-646A-RF in all correspondence. Responses are due by 12/14/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. title: MH-60R/S Planned Maintenance Interval (PMI) in Rota, Spain
description: DESCRIPTION: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) is seeking qualified sources that can provide commercial Depot-level Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) services for the United States Navy (USN) MH-60R/S helicopters at Naval Station (NS) Rota, Spain. The support includes Planned Maintenance Interval (PMI) and In Service Repair (ISR) of the MH-60R and MH-60S aircraft in accordance with the H-60 Integrated Maintenance Plan (IMP). Specific performance requirements include planning, managing, and organizing internal controls which will require furnishing all necessary personnel, access to facilities, equipment, materials, supplies, testing equipment, and management to rework, overhaul, and test items to conform to the IMP and established Turnaround Times (TATs). It is anticipated the Government will award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with a one-year base period and four (4) one-year option periods. This market research tool is being utilized to identify capable firms, of all sizes, prior to finalizing the method of acquisition. This notice should not be construed as a formal solicitation or an obligation on the part of the Government of the United States to acquire any parts or services. Any information provided to the Government is strictly voluntary and at no cost to the Government. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The contractor will be required to perform MH-60R/S PMI in alignment with PMA-299 IMP on approximately two to four (2-4) aircraft per year onboard NS Rota, Spain. The anticipated total annual aircraft inductions is an estimate only and subject to change during development of this requirement These PMI events include all MH-60R/S requirements outlined in A1-H60-IMP-000, inspection bulletin compliance, and conducting preventive, corrective, and investigative maintenance. Additionally, completion of Technical Directive (TD) incorporation, In Service Repair (ISR), and maintenance to facilitate Intermediate (I) and Organizational (O) Level requirements will be required. PMI and ISR work include both scheduled and unscheduled requirements: 1. Scheduled Maintenance: PMI-1N and PMI-2N requirement includes airframe, systems, and component inspection through visual and Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) methods, defect correction, preventative maintenance, operational checkouts, and Technical Directive compliance. The required TAT thresholds for PMI-1N and PMI-2N are 120 and 135 calendar days, respectively. The IMP requirements for aircraft subject to this process are the minimum requirements, formulated and established to the depth required to ensure the reliability, operational availability, safe operation and airworthiness of the aircraft for the duration of the established service period. The IMP will provide depot support throughout the total service life of the aircraft. 2. Unscheduled Maintenance: Unscheduled Maintenance are the tasks that are not related to a specific IMP Scheduled Maintenance requirement and is further divided into 4 subcategories: a. Over and above (O&A) O&A tasks are repairs performed concurrent with a PMI event. Refer to the Defense Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) 252.217-7028 for a thorough description of Over and Above Work. b. In-Service Repairs (ISR) ISR requests are for depot-level repairs on inducted and non-inducted aircraft. ISR work may require the Contractor to dispatch personnel as a contractor field service team (CFT) to perform aircraft repairs at remote locations. c. Customer Service Request (CSR) CSR requests come from operational fleet or the MH-60R/S T/M/S program office for both inducted and non-inducted aircraft. CSR requirements include, but are not limited to Organizational and Intermediate level maintenance. CSR work may require the Contractor to dispatch personnel as a CFT to perform aircraft repairs at remote locations. d. Depot-Level Technical Directives (TD) TD (aircraft modification and bulletins) shall be accomplished either concurrently with PMI events or as standalone actions. The Government will normally provide technical directive kits, special materials, and special Support Equipment (SE) required for completing modifications. Base and Facility Access: All Contractor personnel must be eligible for and obtain perpetual base access at NS Rota, Spain for the duration of the contract. This requires submitting all necessary documentation for a Tarjeta Especial de Identificacion (TEI) to be granted base access in accordance with host nation and base security statutes. To obtain TEI all required forms must be submitted for each employee 60 days prior (and then annually 60 days before expiration, or more frequently as required by base and host nation statutes). As part of this requirement, the contractor must provide insurance from a company listed on an EU Mercantile Registry and documented on a Certificate of Insurance. CAPABILITIES STATEMENT REQUIREMENTS: Interested responsible sources are requested to submit a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 12 pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum) demonstrating ability to perform the tasking listed under the required capabilities by addressing the following: Company Name, Address, Business Size, and Point-of-Contact (POC) Name, Phone Number, Fax Number, and Email Address. Company Profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), UEI Number, Cage Code Number, and a statement regarding current small/other than small business status. Prior and current corporate experience performing aircraft maintenance or MRO services of similar size and scope to the tasking described under �Required Capabilities� within the last three (3) years, including a brief description of how the referenced contract or effort relates to those tasks. Management approach to staffing this effort with qualified technical personnel in an overseas environment. Company�s ability to begin performance upon contract award. Whether the company has managed a team of subcontractors before, with details, including contracts and teaming arrangements. An explanation of the specific technical skills the company possesses which ensures capability to perform the tasks. Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) and Host-Nation Operational Experience: Detail experience executing aviation depot-level maintenance or similar complex technical tasks specifically within the Kingdom of Spain, including compliance with the U.S.-Spain Agreement on Defense Cooperation (ADC), Spanish labor laws, and base access protocols at military installations such as NS Rota, Spain. If your company does not possess direct experience operating in Spain, detail your experience managing similar aviation depot-level maintenance tasks in other OCONUS environments, specifically addressing your corporate capability, timeline, and mitigation strategy to establish host-nation legal compliance and base access within the required schedule constraints. The U.S. Government will provide special tooling including MH-60 Peculiar and Common SE, and Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) as Government-Furnished Property (GFP) for this effort. Describe your firm�s capability to provide common contractor-furnished hand tools, Individual Material Readiness List (IMRL) items, and any logistical approach to managing the inventory and calibration requirements of the GFP on-site. Execution of PMI-2N requires a certified aircraft strip and paint facility capable of housing H-60 aircraft located at NS Rota. The U.S. Government does not own such a facility. Please provide documented evidence of your firm's current access to, or lease of, a certified aircraft paint and strip booth at NS Rota, that is approved for use on military aircraft. title: Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV
description: Pesulakoneiden toimitukset ja asennukset sekä huoltotoiminnot / VAV Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien kiinteistöjen pesuloiden ja kuivaushuoneiden uusien koneiden toimituksiin, asennuksiin sekä niiden huoltotoimintoihin. Tarkemmin tiloihin ja laitekantaan voi tutustua oheisesta kohdeluettelosta. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden koneuusintoihin liittyviä toimeksiantoja esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 60 kpl / vuosi. Tilastojen mukaan pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden konehuoltoihin liittyviä vikatarkastus-/korjauksia esiintyisi tässä kiinteistökannassa noin 360 kpl / vuosi, jonka lisäksi Tilaajalla on ennakoivaa vuosihuoltotoimintaa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta. Tilaaja ei sitoudu hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Tilaaja pitää erityisen tärkeänä, että pesula- ja kuivaushuoneissa käytettävät koneet huolletaan systemaattisesti ("vuosihuollot"). Lisäksi arjessa esiintyvät muunlaiset vikakorjaukset tehdään ripeästi ja että koneet uusitaan elinkaariajattelu huomioiden kustannustehokkaasti. Uusien pesulakoneiden toimituksissa ja asennuksissa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Pesula- ja kuivaushuoneiden laitekannan uusiminen Tilaajan kanssa erikseen sopien Pesulakoneiden huoltotoiminnassa palveluun kuuluu mm.: • Laitteiden ennakoiva vuosihuoltotoiminta • Kuivausrummun huoltotoimet vikaantumisissa • Pesukoneen poisto-/tuloputken huollot, virran antoon liittyvien vikojen selvittely ja ohjauspaneelien huolto-/ korjaustoimet • Mankelin erilaiset huolto-/korjaustoimet • Kuivaushuoneen puhaltimien virhetilanteiden hoitaminen Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Palvelu toteutetaan tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja laatuvaatimusten mukaisesti. Tarjoajan antama tarjous on sitova. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. EU-kynnysarvon ylittävässä hankinnassa sopimus voidaan tehdä aikaisintaan 14 vuorokauden kuluttua siitä, kun Tarjoaja on saanut tai hänen katsotaan saaneen päätöksen perusteluineen tiedoksi. Tarjoaja ei saa esittää esimerkiksi omissa tarjousasiakirjoissaan ehtoja, jotka vaikuttaisivat hankintasopimuksen sisältöön. Sopimuskauden tavoitealkamisajankohta on 1.4.2027 ja sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi.,

title: Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal
description: 30 OCT 2026 The response due date is 4:00 PM CST on 14 DEC 2026. Submit responses to this request for partnership solutions to debby.c.broyles.civ@army.mil and heather.b.johns.civ@army.mil with subject line: PSO Response Production of Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Lethality Payloads at Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). Partnership Solutions Opening � Request for Whitepapers Agency: Department of War (DoW) / Army Materiel Command (AMC) Notice Type: Partnership Solutions Opening (PSO) Title: Production of sUAS Lethality Payloads at PBA. 1.0 INTRODUCTION & AUTHORITY The U.S. Army Materiel Command (AMC) is issuing this request for partnership solutions via white paper submission solely for market research, planning, and concept exploration regarding a potential Public-Private Partnership (P3) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 7544. The Government is requesting specific conceptual solutions on how to optimally structure and execute P3 Cooperative Arrangements. The core objective is to leverage private investment to modernize Government facilities to Industry 4.0 and 5.0 automation standards. Industry 4.0 is defined as the Fourth Industrial Revolution, is characterized by the "Smart Factory." It aims to create highly efficient, autonomous production lines by integrating cyber-physical systems with the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing. Industry 5.0 is not meant to replace Industry 4.0 but to refine it. It recognizes that pure automation can overlook human creativity and environmental impact. It places the well-being of the worker and the planet at the center of the industrial process. This modernization will enable authorized co-production and facility-use activities that mutually benefit the Government's national security mission and the private partner's commercial enterprise. Disclaimer: This PSO does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), nor is it a procurement action governed by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). The Government is not obligated to enter into any cooperative arrangement or agreement because of this PSO and will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submitting a response. 2.0 PROBLEM STATEMENT PBA is requesting a commercial partnership to support the development and production of lethal energetic payloads for sUAS and Electronic Safe & Arming Devices (ESAD). These efforts include scaling low-cost, modernized sUAS lethality and energetic payload manufacturing. PBA intends for flexible production lines with ability to accommodate modular manufacturing capabilities for differing explosives, varying payload sizes, explosive safe and arming devices, energetic airframes, etc. PBA can provide both logistical and facility support, including approximately 100,000 square feet of storage and production capacity. The government has various 1 or 2 story buildings available in area 34-000 ranging in size from 396 sq ft to 13,551 sq ft with various existing capabilities to include electricity, water, air sewer, Natural Gas, and/or steam. Additional building details provided in Attachment 1. The production facilities were constructed in 1941-42 for the war effort to handle highly volatile chemical, pyrotechnic, and incendiary compounds. Structurally and architecturally, these buildings reflect a combination of standardized strict hazard segmentation, and fortified safety engineering. Buildings are constructed with heavy, reinforced concrete interior blast walls and thick foundations, but with deliberately weak, lightweight exterior walls and roofs. PBA can provide the following support: � Direct labor � Engineering � Base operations � Logistical support � Environmental and safety support, including leveraging PBA's existing Explosive Site Safety Plans to expedite the mandatory joint site-licensing updates required for the partner's specific energetic footprint and, as applicable, for any non-Department of Defense owned toxic or hazardous materials, supporting Government coordination and processing of a 10 U.S.C. 2692 exception request; the contractor remains responsible for providing the technical, environmental, safety, and operational information required to support that request. � Utilities: Existing utility systems vary by facility as shown in Attachment 1. The contractor is responsible for any necessary capital investments required to utilize these utilities, including the procurement and installation of utility meters, sub-meters, service hookups, and distribution lines. 3.0 FINANCIAL & INVESTMENT REQUIREMENTS (CAPITAL EXPENDITURES) To accelerate modernization without requiring upfront Government funding, the selected industry partner(s) must meet the following financial parameters: Private Equity Financed Capital Expenditures (CapEx): An industry partner(s) must utilize private equity or internal corporate capital to fund 100% of the modernization CapEx for the targeted building(s). Scope of CapEx: This investment must cover all necessary facility upgrades, structural modifications, equipment procurement, software integration, and physical installation. Permanent upgrades become Government property upon installation, with the contractor retaining operational use for the duration of the agreement. 4.0 OPERATIONAL CONCEPT: COOPERATIVE ARRANGEMENT In exchange for the capital investment, the Government will enter a Cooperative Arrangement pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 7544(a). Commercial Capacity Guarantee (Facilities Use): In accordance with 10 U.S.C 7544(b)(5), an industry partner will be granted a facilities-use contract guaranteeing a portion of the capacity of the modernized/new lines for their own commercial requirements, with the precise amount to be negotiated based on the overall structure of the partnership, other in-kind considerations offered, etc. Excess Capacity Utilization: Pursuant to 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(3), an industry partner is authorized to use any additional excess capacity not actively utilized or identified for future by the Government. Non-Interference Mandate: As required by 10 U.S.C 7544(c)(2), all commercial production must not interfere with the performance of work for the Department of War. Build-to-Operate (BTO) Model: To accelerate modernization, the cooperative arrangement may utilize a BTO framework. The industry partner will develop, locate, and temporarily operate innovative technological capabilities at OIB sites until they recover their initial capital investment and realize an agreed upon profit. Upon reaching this threshold, operational control transitions to the OIB for long term sustainment, allowing the contractor to refocus on next generation innovation. This BTO model benefits the enterprise by optimizing both sectors' strengths and yields faster capability deployment during the innovation phase and steadier, modernized sustainment production within the OIB. 5.0 MANDATORY STATUTORY PROVISIONS (10 U.S.C. 7544) Indemnification: A selected Industry partner will be required to agree to the indemnity restrictions located at 10 U.S.C. 7544(c)(4). Suspension/Termination: The Government may suspend or terminate commercial activity, or require priority performance for military work, during a war or national emergency. 6.0 PARTNERSHIP PROCESS 6.1 Phase I: Initial Whitepaper Submission Submission: Respondents shall submit an initial written whitepaper addressing the requirements outlined in Section 7.0 (Volumes I, II, and III). Initial submissions must be received within 45 days of the publication of this PSO (no later than 4:00 PM CST on the designated date). Assessment: The Government will assess all timely submissions against the attributes identified in Section 8.0 (Technological Innovation, Financial Viability, and OIB Utilization). 6.2 Phase II: PBA On-Site Visit & Technical Exchange Invitation: The most highly assessed whitepaper respondents will receive a formal invitation detailing the schedule and protocol for a mandatory on-site visit at Pine Bluff Arsenal. title: Energetic Material and Ordnance Research and Development RFI
description: This Request for Information will outline the overarching objectives for the Research and Development of mission effects technologies that the Contractor may perform for the AFRL Mission Effects Division (AFRL/RAB) in the broadest and most flexible manner for the USAF. AFRL/RAB directs and conducts basic, exploratory and advanced research and development of fuzes, warheads, energetic materials, AI & decision-making, and weapon algorithm development. The objective of this research is to identify promising energetic material systems that can mature to transition into a larger, focused project while also identifying and exploring new energetic materials, new processing methods for producing energetic materials, and formulate those new materials that expand the frontiers in survivability, controlled output, multi-functionality, power density, and insensitivity. This research encompasses the synthesis, scale-up, production, processing, machining, and characterization of advanced energetic materials.

title: Denmark, Greenland, Faroes – Echo, ultrasound and doppler imaging equipment – Fællesregionalt udbud efter ultralydsudstyr
description: Dette udbud er efter rammeaftaler på ultralydsudstyr til alle kliniske specialer. Der efterspørges udstyr i to kvalitetsklasser, Guld og Sølv. Udbuddet er et fælleudbud, med forpligtende deltagelse fra de fem regioner, samt option på deltagelse fra Grønland og Færøerne. Der er 14 delaftaler, fordelt på 7 specialer og 2 kvalitetsklasser. Det indgås parallelle rammeaftaler med 3-4 vindere i hver delaftale, indplaceret i en prioriteret rækkefølge. Aftræk vil ske fra 1. vinderen, medmindre der er konkrete kliniske grunde til at vælge en af de efterstående vindere. En Tilbudsgiver kan tilbyde og vinde placeringer i flere delaftaler, men kun byde med en apparat konfiguration til hver af de 14 delaftaler.

title: Udbud af dynamisk indkøbssystem vedrørende bygherrerådgivning på vand- og spildevandsområdet
description: Hillerød Vand A/S og Hillerød Spildevand A/S udbyder et dynamisk indkøbssystem vedrørende bygherrerådgivning. Rådgivningen kan omfatte bygherrerådgivning i forbindelse med planlægning, udbud og gennemførelse af projekter på vand- og spildevandsområdet, herunder: - Projektmodning, behovsafklaring og udarbejdelse af beslutningsgrundlag. - Fastlæggelse af bygherrens krav til funktion, kvalitet, økonomi, drift og dokumentation. - Udbuds- og kontraheringsbistand ved valg af rådgivere og entreprenører. - Projektstyring, herunder opfølgning på økonomi, tidsplan, risici og ændringer. - Projektgranskning, kvalitetssikring og koordinering mellem projektets parter. - Bistand ved aflevering, mangelopfølgning, idriftsættelse og overgang til drift. Rådgivningen kan desuden omfatte særskilt beskrevne ydelser vedrørende blandt andet forundersøgelser, myndighedsforhold, interessentinddragelse, digitale leverancer, bæredygtighed, arbejdsmiljøkoordinering, byggeledelse og fagtilsyn. Der henvises i øvrigt til udbudsmaterialet for en mere detaljeret beskrivelse.

title: Germany – Primary school construction work – Übernahme der Funktion der Bauherrschaft für das Projekt Erweiterung, Generalsanierung und Umbau der Grundschule Elbach
description: 1. Baumaßnahme: Gegenstand des Projekts ist die Erweiterung, Generalsanierung und der Umbau der Grundschule Elbach. Das Projektgrundstück mit der Flurnummer 782/1 der Gemarkung Hundham hat die Anschrift Steingrabenstraße 3, 83730 Fischbachau-Dürnbach. Es liegt am Ortsrand und befindet sich im Eigentum des Auftraggebers. Das Projektgrundstück ist erschlossen; es hat Hanglage, liegt auf einem nach Westen abfallenden Hang. Die vorhandene Schulanlage besteht aus einem 3-geschoßigen Altbau (Baujahr ca. 1960) und einem 2-geschoßigem Querbau mit Sporthalle (beide Baujahr 1993). Der Altbau ist im Hinblick auf sein Alter sanierungsbedürftig. Der Querbau befindet sich technisch und funktional in einem zeitgemäßen Zustand. Die Bestandsbauten sind kein Baudenkmale und unterliegen auch nicht dem Ensembleschutz. Die vorhandene Schulanlage soll durch einen Erweiterungsbau mit Anschluss an den Bestand erweitert werden. Gemäß dem behördlich genehmigten Raumprogramm soll die Schule zu einer 3-zügigen Schule mit offener Ganztagsbetreuung erweitert werden. Vorhandene Defizite in Bezug auf Flächen, Organisation und Zuordnung der Räume werden dabei behoben, der Altbau generalsaniert und die Schule durch Erweiterung, Umbau und Modernisierung zukunftsfähig für die nächsten Jahrzehnte gemacht. Um das Raumprogramm umsetzen zu können, müssen 841 m² HNF – was zu einer BGF von ca. 1.500 m² führt – neu geschaffen werden, da im Bestand keine nennenswerten Flächenreserven vorhanden sind. Die Gesamtmaßnahme soll in mehreren Bauabschnitten wie folgt realisiert werden: 1. Errichtung des Erweiterungsbaus mit Anschluss an das Bestandsgebäude; 2. Generalsanierung des Altbaus mit temporärer Verlagerung der vorhandenen Nutzungen in Quer- und Neubaugebäude; 3. Arbeiten am Querbau. 2. Planungsstand: Der Auftraggeber hat bereits Planungs- und Ingenieurleistungen für die Realisierung des Projekts in Auftrag gegeben, unter anderem Objektplanungsleistungen für Gebäude und Innenräume sowie Fachplanungsleistungen der Technischen Ausrüstung und Tragwerksplanung. Derzeitiger Planungsstand für die vorgenannten Leistungen ist die HOAI-Leistungsphase 3. Die Gesamtmaßnahme soll baulich spätestens am 13.06.2031 abgeschlossen werden. Der Erweiterungsbau soll bereits am 06.06.2029 fertiggestellt sein. 3. Projektkosten: Der Auftraggeber geht derzeit von Projektkosten für die Gesamtmaßnahme von 11.840.464,04 Euro brutto aus (Kostenschätzung Stand 21.04.2026, KG 200 bis 700). Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, für das Bauvorhaben Fördermittel zu erlangen. Es liegen bereits entsprechende Bewilligungs-, Zuwendungs- und Zuweisungsbescheide vor. 4. Leistungen des Auftragnehmers: Der Auftragnehmer wird als Geschäftsbesorger tätig und übernimmt in dieser Funktion für den Auftraggeber vollumfänglich die Funktion und Aufgaben der Bauherrschaft für das Projekt. Der Auftragnehmer wird das Projekt auf Grundlage und in Fortführung der vorhandene Planungsergebnisse in Abstimmung mit dem Auftraggeber realisieren. Der Auftragnehmer übernimmt hierbei insbesondere die kaufmännische und finanzwirtschaftliche Betreuung des Projekts sowie Projektsteuerungs- und Finanzierungsdienstleistungen und sorgt für die Erbringung aller erforderlicher Planungsleistungen ab der HOAI-Leistungsphase 5 – dies durch Vertragsübernahme vorbehaltlich der Zustimmung des jeweiligen Planungsbüros, soweit bereits Planung-/Ingenieurverträge durch den Auftraggeber abgeschlossen wurden – und zudem für die Erbringung der Bauleistungen für das Projekt.

description: Försvarsmakten befinner sig i en tillväxtperiod och etablerar verksamhet på flera nya orter, där nya fordonsverkstäder byggs och tas i drift. Däck- och hjulunderhåll är en central del av verkstädernas dagliga verksamhet, liksom annan service och annat underhåll av fordon. Upphandlingen omfattar utrustning för däck- och hjulhantering till både personbilar och lastbilar/tunga fordon: däckmonterare, balanseringsmaskiner, hjultvättar och hjullyftar samt balanseringsvikter och förbrukningsmaterial. Den omfattar också fyrhjulsmätare för personbil och lastbil. Dessutom ingår annan verkstadsutrustning: induktionsvärmare, bromsverktyg (bland annat universella kolvbackningsverktyg för bromsok), AC-stationer, spilloljeskålar/gropvagnar, mobila extraktionsenheter för bränsle och växellådstvättar. Ramavtalet ska dels utrusta de nya verkstäderna i takt med att de färdigställs, dels ge befintliga verkstäder redundans och löpande försörjning när uttjänt utrustning byts ut. Syftet med upphandlingen är att säkra försörjningstryggheten inom området. Försvarsmakten behöver kunna köpa ny utrustning löpande och med kort varsel, till exempel vid haveri, när materiel är uttjänt eller när behoven ökar, utan att göra en ny upphandling varje gång. Ett ramavtal med god leveransförmåga är en förutsättning för att verkstäderna ska kunna behålla sin förmåga över tid, även vid höjd beredskap.
